newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks seen to hit new highs on IMF loan.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks seen to hit new highs on IMF loan.

text.p: Pakistan's stock market is likely to test new highs after the International Monetary Fund agreed on Thursday to a new medium-term loan facility of at least $1.6 billion for Pakistan, analysts said.

IMF's Middle East director Paul Chabrier told a news conference in Islamabad that the loan would be a mix of an enhanced structural adjustment facility (ESAF) and an extended Fund facility, with ESAF forming the major part.
Stock analysts said the market was poised for a take-off amid fresh inflows of foreign portfolio investment but might first consolidate on previous gains.
"This is very positive and the loan is higher than what the market expected," Anisur Rehman, research head at SocGen-Crosby Securities, told Reuters.
Pakistan has been negotiating with the IMF for a $1.2-1.5 billion, three-year ESAF for balance of payments support.
But Chabrier said the amount, to be finalised by the IMF's executive board, would not be less than $1.6 billion. "So it is a little bit more than what was being reported in the press."
Rehman said the higher loan amount showed the IMF's commitment to and confidence in the government and its economic policies.
"We do not have the breakdown or the interest rates at which the loan would be available, but what is more important is...how much the IMF is willing to support," he said.
Sameer Ahmed, head of sales at ING Baring Securities, said the market would surge on the news, but might slow down to consolidate in the immediate term.
"The market will shoot, but should consolidate to around 1,850 and 1,900 points' level, which will be a healthy sign," Ahmed said, adding: "It has come up too far too fast."
The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index on Thursday swung widely both ways before ending 36.12 points higher to 1,985.25 at 0908 GMT in response to the IMF news.
On Tuesday, the index surged 104.06 points, or 5.44 percent, to close at a 30-month high of 2,016.51, but dropped 3.34 percent to 1,949.13 points on Wednesday amid profit-taking.
Rehman said the IMF support could help the index achieve new highs in the next few months on the back of renewed foreign fund buying.
"A lot of (foreign) fund managers were waiting, making sure that the ESAF is in and the IMF commitment is there.

"Now we can see huge inflows from large U.S.-based funds coming to Pakistan, which can take the index to new highs," he said. He added that the index was likely to surge above the 2,300-point level in three months.

Analysts said PTCL and Hub Power would continue to lead the market, but other blue chips with large market capitalisation and some of the second-tier stocks would start rising as funds spill over from market leaders.
